issues.legal_issue: A decree for eviction that became unenforceable because of a statutory bar revives and becomes executable when a later retrospective amendment removes that bar, if the decree was not set aside.
material_facts: A landlord obtained an eviction decree against a tenant, and the decree became final without an appeal or revision.
During execution, the tenant objected that the court which had passed the decree lacked jurisdiction; the executing court consequently treated the decree as inexecutable.
A later amendment applied the relevant jurisdictional provision retrospectively and provided for the validity of affected decisions.
The landlord applied to revive and execute the decree, and the executing court allowed the application; the High Court dismissed the tenant’s revision.
issues.conclusion: The decree had not been set aside; it had only become dormant and inexecutable. Once the retrospective amendment removed the bar, the decree revived and became executable. The courts below were correct, and the appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Section 9 of the U.P. Urban Buildings (Regulation of Letting, Rent and Eviction) Act, 1972, as applied by section 26(6) of the 1976 Amendment Act, and the relevant provisions of section 26, were interpreted to give effect to the retrospective change and revive decrees that had become inexecutable. Applying the doctrine of eclipse, the Court held that a decree merely rendered inoperative by a legal bar is not thereby set aside and may become operative when the bar is removed. The Court relied on Bhikaji Narain Dhakras v. State of Madhya Pradesh, Deep Chand v. State of U.P., Mahendra Lal Jaini v. State of Uttar Pradesh, S. Anbalagan v. B. Devarajan, and Kailash Sonkar v. Smt. Maya Devi.

rule.if: execution_challenge and prior_ejectment_decree_remained_on_record and decree_was_only_inexecutable and retroactive_change_removed_execution_bar

predicates.execution_challenge: The proceeding challenged the revival or execution of an eviction decree.
predicates.prior_ejectment_decree_remained_on_recor: A decree for eviction had been made and had not been set aside or removed from the record.
predicates.decree_was_only_inexecutable: A legal impediment prevented execution of the decree without invalidating or setting it aside.
predicates.retroactive_change_removed_execution_bar: A later change in the law applied retrospectively and removed the impediment to executing the decree.

issues.definition: When an execution challenge concerns an eviction decree that remained on record but was only inexecutable, and a retrospective legal change removes the execution bar, the decree revives and becomes executable.
